results.title: How war in the Middle East is disrupting medical supply chains - pharmaphorum
results.content:
## Impact on shipping and air freight

The Middle East is a vital part of the international air freight network. According to the International Air Transport Association, the region accounted for 13.2% of world air cargo in January 2026, before the war.

The conflict quickly and sharply disrupted air freight. Because many planes can no longer safely fly over Iranian or nearby airspace, they have been forced to divert to longer alternative routes that take more time and use more fuel. At the same time, average jet fuel prices have surged. They are up more than 100% over the past month, according to the International Air Transport Association's (IATA) latest fuel price monitor. As a result, air freight rates on key routes between Asia and Europe have risen by as much as 70%. [...] " property="og:image"> " property="og:image:url">

Developing Asia and the Pacific (DAP) is highly

strait through its reliance on imported oil and
gas from the Persian Gulf, with spillovers from
energy prices, shipping, aviation and financial
markets.

Inflation in DAP is projected at 3.6% in 2026
and 3.4% in 2027 in the early stabilization
scenario but could rise to 5.6% in 2026 if
tensions in the Middle East remain through the

results.title: US Import Volumes Hold Steady Despite Iran War, but Cost Pressures Concern Retailers - WWD
results.content:
“Just because retailers don’t import a lot of merchandise from the Middle East doesn’t mean the U.S. supply chain isn’t affected by the turmoil there,” said Jonathan Gold, vice president for supply chain and customs policy at the NRF. “The supply chain is global and disruptions anywhere along it can have ripple effects whether it’s rerouting of vessels, equipment out of position, higher fuel costs for shippers or rising gas prices that leave less money in consumers’ pockets.”

According to Gold, retailers are monitoring the situation daily and working with their transportation partners to minimize any impact.

Hackett Associates founder Ben Hackett said it is “too soon” to measure the impact of Tuesday night’s two-week ceasefire. [...] SJ Newsletters
